title: Azure SQL Database Overview
description: Understand Azure SQL Database tiers, purchasing models, and how they fit ASP.NET Core apps.

data.text: Azure SQL Database is a fully managed relational database engine based on SQL Server. It handles patching, backups, high availability, and scaling, so you can focus on data and C# code.

rows: Fully managed database with its own resources
Many small databases with variable usage
Near-full SQL Server compatibility in Azure

items: **General Purpose** — balanced compute and storage for most apps
**Business Critical** — in-memory OLTP and high IO for latency-sensitive apps
**Hyperscale** — automatically scales storage up to hundreds of terabytes

data.title: Start small
data.text: Begin with General Purpose and serverless compute. You can scale up or switch tiers later with minimal downtime.

data.title: Create an Azure SQL logical server and database
data.content: Use the Azure CLI to create the database infrastructure.
data.code:
az sql server create \
  --name aspnet-azure-sql \
  --resource-group azure-for-aspnet-rg \
  --location eastus \
  --admin-user sqladmin \
  --admin-password 'YourSecurePassword123!'

az sql db create \
  --name BlogDb \
  --server aspnet-azure-sql \
  --resource-group azure-for-aspnet-rg \
  --service-objective GP_S_Gen5_2

items.question: Is Azure SQL the same as SQL Server?
items.answer: It uses the same engine, but Azure SQL Database is a managed service with different networking, backup, and tuning behaviors.

items.question: Can I use Entity Framework Core with Azure SQL?
items.answer: Yes. EF Core works with Azure SQL the same way it works with on-premises SQL Server.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure SQL Database is a managed relational database based on SQL Server
Start with General Purpose serverless for cost-effective development
Use single databases for new apps and managed instances for migrations
Connection strings and firewall rules are configured separately from the database
data.takeaway: Azure SQL removes database administration overhead while keeping the familiar SQL Server programming model for C# developers.
